Height increases upward, the right-bottom strand is the overstrand under the determinant crossing convention, and the labels at the ends record the ordered parenthesizations; no proof below relies on the drawing.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Choose pairwise disjoint balls around the $n$ singular points so each resolved pair of branches is monotone in height inside its ball. The same height function is used on every resolution, so $r(K_\epsilon)=r$ for all $\epsilon$. If necessary, move the singular knot by an isotopy supported in the balls to separate the singular heights and make the crossings monotone; each corresponding resolution is carried by the same ambient isotopy, so [F6] leaves $\Delta^n I(K)$ unchanged.

Expand the degree-$m$ part of $\Delta^n I(K)$ as a finite sum of pairing integrals over the resolution choices. If a pairing has no chord endpoint in the $i$th crossing ball, its integrand and diagram are independent of the sign $\epsilon_i$, because the two resolved knots agree outside that ball. Summing over $\epsilon_i=+1,-1$ therefore cancels that term. Hence every nonzero contribution to the $n$-fold difference must meet each of the $n$ balls.

Apply the principal-symbol theorem [F7] to the common singular Morse presentation. It gives $D_nZ(K)_m=0$ for $m<n$ and $D_nZ(K)_n=D$. The local hypotheses hold by step 1.1 and the unframed target agrees by [F2, F3].

For one singular point, let $w_\pm(t)=z_{1,\pm}(t)-z_{2,\pm}(t)$ be the relative complex coordinate of its two monotone branches in the positive and negative resolutions. The loop obtained by following $w_+$ and then the reverse of $w_-$ winds once positively around $0$: the two resolutions are the opposite half-turns of the relative vector. Hence $\frac1{2\pi i}\left(\int d\log w_+-\int d\log w_-\right)=1$. For two upward branches this is the difference of angular changes $+\pi-(-\pi)=2\pi$. Reversing both branch orientations leaves the determinant sign unchanged and changes the down count by two; reversing exactly one branch reverses both the crossing sign and the factor $(-1)^{\downarrow}$. Thus under [F4] the coefficient is $+1$ for every oriented positive resolution. The localization theorem [F7] identifies this local winding contribution with the leading term of the full one-singular tangle. Thus the leading term is the one-chord diagram joining the two preimages.

The degree-$n$ diagram in [F7] pairs exactly the two preimages of each marked double point. Step 3.1 checks that its coefficient has sign $+1$ under the present oriented resolution convention. Local factors compose in height order, and their endpoints occur on the original circle skeleton; hence the resulting class is precisely $D$ in the unframed 4T+1T quotient. This agrees with the full principal-symbol assertion in step 2.1, including diagrams that vanish under 1T.

The common factor $Z(H)^{-r}$ can be pulled outside the alternating sum because all resolutions have the same $r$. Its degree-zero coefficient is $1$, so multiplication by it preserves the first nonzero homogeneous component: the degree-$n$ component remains $D$, and all lower degrees remain zero. For $n=0$, the alternating sum is $I(K)$ and its degree-zero coefficient is $1$ by [F2]. Thus $\Delta^n I(K)=D+\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{>n}$ in every case.

Cut at regular levels outside those neighborhoods. For the regular pieces of the Stokes argument, consider a compact tangle $T_s$ without critical points, with fixed boundary points and parameter $s\in[0,1]$. On a compactified branch chamber, write the full degree-$m$ form as the finite sum $\omega_m=\sum_P(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]\bigwedge_{j=1}^m d\log(z_j-z'_j)$, with each differential taken in the level and deformation variables. Every branch difference is nonzero because the tangle is embedded and has no critical points; hence each logarithmic factor is closed and $d\omega_m=0$. Stokes on the chamber cylinder reduces equality of the two end integrals to vanishing on its codimension-one faces.

The upper and lower closure caps lie in height bands disjoint from $T$ and the return arc. Each cap has exactly two points at every regular level in its band. In a nonempty pairing on an upper cap, the chord at the highest selected level has an empty subarc on the cap side; on a lower cap use the chord at the lowest selected level. In either case that chord is isolated, so [F4] kills the diagram. The return arc has exactly one point at each level of $[a,b]$, so it has no internal pairing. Hence cap and return factors contribute only their degree-zero units.

On an outer-level face, the extreme endpoints are fixed, so the restricted form has no $ds$ component and vanishes. On a face where adjacent levels coincide, if the two chords use the same two branches, their logarithmic forms agree and their wedge is zero. If they use four distinct branches, exchanging the two chord choices preserves the diagram and reverses the wedge sign, so the terms cancel in pairs. If they use exactly three branches, the 4T relation [F4] groups the six choices into one common diagram coefficient times $\alpha_{12}\wedge\alpha_{23}+\alpha_{23}\wedge\alpha_{31}+\alpha_{31}\wedge\alpha_{12}$, where $\alpha_{ij}=d\log(z_i-z_j)$. Setting $f=z_1-z_2$, $g=z_2-z_3$, and $z_3-z_1=-(f+g)$, direct expansion gives the coefficient $1/(fg)-1/(g(f+g))-1/(f(f+g))=0$. A codimension-one center is an adjacent-level face already handled above. Thus the only remaining boundary integrals are the two ends $s=0,1$, which are equal. Summing the finitely many chambers proves invariance for the stated regular fixed-boundary tangle. The closed-knot conclusion across critical levels is the explicitly imported result [F6].

Put $M=\sup_T|z|$ and take $R>M+1$. Any chord using the return arc over $[a,b]$ joins $R$ to $z\in T$ and has factor $dz/(z-R)$. Choose finitely many small critical bands of the fixed $T$, with one critical point in each, and regular bands covering the rest. In a critical band write $t=c\pm s^2$. The colliding branches satisfy $z_\pm(s)=z_c\pm v s+O(s^2)$ with $v\ne0$, so their short-chord factor is bounded in absolute value by $C\,ds/s$. Every other pair of fixed branches has a nonzero limiting separation and hence a factor bounded by $C\,ds$, after shrinking the band.
